title: Tenant soft-isolation, adaptive burst quotas and autoscale smoothing for Dedicated
creator: Ava Martinez
overview: Problem: Customers on Dedicated occasionally encounter noisy tenants that cause transient latency spikes or cost overruns for other tenants in the same pool. Current soft-burst behavior is manual and lacks telemetry-driven headroom management. Proposal: introduce a tenant-level soft-isolation model (soft-reserve + adaptive burst escrow) that provides configurable minimum capacity, an on-demand burst escrow that is replenished and reclaimed by policy, and autoscale smoothing to reduce oscillation between reserve and burst modes. The feature will be controllable via API and Console, observable in the Console's per-tenant dashboard, and interoperable with existing fallback and capacity routing policies.
problem_statement: Dedicated pools must balance utilization and predictable latency for paying tenants. We need a mechanism that lets tenants safely burst above their reservation without risking noisy-neighbor degradation for others, while preserving economic utilization. The current model is either too rigid (fixed reservation) or too permissive (unbounded burst) with insufficient telemetry and reclaim guarantees.
goals: Provide configurable tenant soft-reservation (min_reserved) that guarantees baseline throughput/latency
Implement an adaptive burst escrow that grants short-term tokens based on historical usage and remaining capacity
Add autoscale smoothing (EWMA-based) to avoid rapid twice-per-minute scale oscillations
Expose controls in REST API and Console plus clear observability (per-tenant cost, burst usage, preemption events)
Enable safe reclaim policies so that preemption is gradual and meet SLAs for critical customers
non_goals: Rewrite the scheduling layer — this PRD augments routing and quota logic, not low-level kernel scheduling
Provide unlimited burst for all tenants — bursts are intentionally bounded by escrow policies
Replace Dedicated pool-level autoscaling; this augments per-tenant controls only
requirements: API: POST/PUT tenant reservation config with fields min_reserved (vCPU-equivalent), burst_escrow_units, reclaim_priority, auto_replenish=true/false
Console: UI for tenant reservation, real-time burst usage timeline, and manual reclaim button
Runtime: tokenized burst escrow evaluated per-tenant; grant if pool headroom >= threshold and escrow balance > 0
Telemetry: emit metrics burst.allocated, burst.reclaimed, reservation.utilization, preemptions.count, p95_latency_per_tenant
Autoscale smoothing: implement EWMA smoothing parameter configurable per-pool, default alpha=0.2
Preemption policy: soft reclaim with 30s negotiated drain, then hard reclaim after configurable grace (default 90s)
Fallback: on reclaim failure, route excess requests to compatible model variant or lower-cost tier per existing routing rules
Integration tests: unit + e2e that simulate noisy-tenant scenarios and chaos preemption
Docs: Console help text, API docs, and runbook for SRE/Oncall
acceptance_criteria: Enable API/config change: tenant min_reserved and burst_escrow accepted and applied in < 2 minutes
Burst allocation only occurs when pool headroom >= 5% of pool capacity (configurable)
After 1h of steady load, escrow replenishment adapts so that average burst granted follows historical 95th percentile usage without exceeding 2x committed reservation
Preemption events: less than 5% of total requests from any tenant may be hard-preempted in a 24h window under simulated noisy neighbor tests
Latency: for tenants with min_reserved configured, p95 tail latency remains within 1.5x of baseline under 1x-3x bursts
Observability: Console shows real-time burst balance and a historical chart; metrics appear in the platform metrics namespace and in the tenant dashboard
Security: all config changes require appropriate RBAC scope and appear in audit logs
E2E tests and chaos runs green in CI and a staged canary run has <1% elevated error rate before full rollout
design_considerations: Tokenized escrow vs fixed bucket: chosen token model for finer-grained reclaim and accounting
Graceful preemption: two-phase approach to reduce tail latency spikes for active requests
Replenishment signal: use sliding 1h window with decay to avoid burst amplification
Cost accounting: attribute burst usage to tenant for billing; include tagging for cost-center reporting
Interoperability: maintain existing fallback model variant compatibility and route priority ordering
tradeoffs: More conservative reclaim delays reduce churn but increase risk of overload for others
Aggressive burst grants improve customer experience but reduce pooled utilization and potential revenue
Telemetry frequency must be balanced: higher frequency gives better control but increases cost and ingest load
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only rollout to SRE and 3 pilot tenants for 2 weeks; collect metrics and adjust EWMA alpha
Beta: opt-in for customers via Console toggle and API; monitor preemptions and billing impact for 4 weeks
Canary: enable by default on 10% of Dedicated pools with rollback capability and kill switch
GA: full rollout in dedicated-2026.04 with migration tool to suggest min_reserved based on historical usage
metrics: per_tenant: burst.allocated.count, burst.reclaimed.count, reservation.utilization, p95_latency, error_rate
SLOs: target p95 latency for reserved tenants; target <5% hard preemptions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: mis-calibrated replenishment leads to frequent preemptions -> Mitigation: conservative default, staged alpha tuning, pilot customers
Risk: billing disputes from burst charges -> Mitigation: clear invoice breakdown and console preview before enabling
Risk: complex controls overwhelm users -> Mitigation: provide sensible defaults and 'auto' mode with telemetry-driven suggestions
Risk: attacker could intentionally oscillate to cause churn -> Mitigation: rate-limit config changes and detect adversarial patterns
